# Best RV power station and solar combo

There's no single winner. The right pick depends on whether you need to run a roof AC. Panel wattage is sold separately for most of these, so match your panels to the station's solar-input limit.

## Top picks

**1. Best for full-time or boondocking, with AC: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous and 8,000W surge. It expands past 12kWh and recharges 0-80% in about 50 minutes from a wall outlet. It's heavy, a two-person lift ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- The older Delta Pro takes up to 1,600W of solar and has a 30A RV outlet ([Outdoor Power Stations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)). I didn't see solar specs for the Pro 3, so check those before buying.

**2. Best mid-range value: BLUETTI AC200L**
- 2,048Wh, 2,400W, up to 1,200W solar input, a built-in 30A RV port, about 62 lb ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- Bluetti generally has the most watt-hours per dollar, but weaker support and a shorter warranty on some models. One source lists 2 years on the AC200P.

**3. Best for weekend trips: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus or Jackery Explorer 1000 v2**
- The DELTA 3 Plus is 1,024Wh with 1,000W solar input, expandable to 5kWh, about 28 lb.
- The Jackery 1000 v2 is 1,070Wh, about 23.8 lb, with a 400W solar cap. It pairs with SolarSaga 100W/200W panels, so two 200W panels use its full input ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).

## Ready-made bundles I can link directly
These are from ALLPOWERS, a lesser-known brand than the big three, with a 400W foldable panel included. Prices were checked 2026-10-27 on ALLPOWERS's store.
- [P1800 (1,024Wh) + 400W panel kit](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-sp037-solar-kit): $731, or $657.90 with code ALLPOWERS26
- [S2000 Pro (1,451Wh) + 400W panel kit](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-s2000-pro-sp037-solar-kit): $963, or $866.70 with code ALLPOWERS26

The code was tested in the cart on 2026-10-25 and expires 2026-12-30. These are affiliate links, so Dealectric earns a commission, but the price is the same for you ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-discount-codes)).

## Sizing
- A 13,500 BTU roof AC draws about 1,500W running and over 3,000W at startup. For AC, you need at least 3,000W of output, like the Pro 3 or Jackery 3000 Pro ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- For a fridge, Starlink, laptop and lights, a 1,000-2,000Wh unit is enough. A 12V fridge plus a Starlink Mini draws about 65W ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)).
- About 300-400W of folding panels refills a mid-size unit in a full day of good sun.

## Caveats
- I couldn't open retailer pages, so I don't have direct buy links for EcoFlow, Bluetti or Jackery. The linked articles have price buttons, but they're affiliate links too. Check current price and specs on the manufacturer's page.
- The EmergencyEnergy article is Ontario-focused. Its US-relevant specs apply, but ignore its Ontario electrical rules.
- Hardwiring to your RV's shore inlet should be done by an electrician. A TT-30 adapter into the inlet is the simple route.

If you tell me your RV's biggest loads (especially AC) and how many days off-grid you want, I can narrow this to one pick.
